messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- INC-2026-009 was an incident in which the scheduler ran the nightly jobs twice on 2026-05-03. [valid 2026-05-08 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-009]
- As of 2025-10-15, the pager for the scheduler rings Team Dune instead of Team Atlas. [valid 2025-10-15 to now; recorded by handover/2025-10-15-scheduler]
- The scheduler deploys on weekday mornings before 11:00 UTC. [constraint; valid 2025-10-27 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-10-27-2]
    earlier: The scheduler deploys on weekdays after 15:00 UTC and at no other time. [constraint; valid 2025-03-19 to 2025-10-27; recorded by standup/ember/2025-03-19]
- INC-2025-004 was an incident affecting the notifier on 2025-02-06. [valid 2025-02-11 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-004]
- INC-2025-023 was an incident affecting the indexer on 2025-10-13. [valid 2025-10-16 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-023]
- INC-2025-017 was an incident affecting the auth gateway on 2025-07-27. [valid 2025-08-01 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-017]
- The root cause of INC-2025-023 was a reindex job that failed silently on a full disk, leaving stale results for two days. [valid 2025-10-16 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-023]
- On 2025-08-01, it was decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead. [decision; valid 2025-08-01 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-017]
- INC-2026-009 happened because two leaders were elected on the scheduler during a network partition. [valid 2026-05-08 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-009]
- The scheduler pulls per-job kill switches from the feature-flags service on every run. [valid 2025-03-28 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2025-03-28]
- INC-2026-003 was an incident in which the webhooks service delivered some events twice on 2026-01-17. [valid 2026-01-22 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-003]
- On 2026-03-09, Team Atlas observed that the scheduler's cold start time tripled after the runtime upgrade. [valid 2026-03-09 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-03-09-2]
- On 2025-06-13, the Ember team decided the scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node. [decision; valid 2025-06-13 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2025-06-13]
- INC-2025-011 was caused by an index missing after the schema migration. [valid 2025-04-28 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-011]
- The root cause of INC-2026-003 was a retry loop that ignored idempotency keys. [valid 2026-01-22 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-003]
- The scheduler's previous single fixed node turned every restart into a missed run. [valid 2025-06-13 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2025-06-13]
- On 2026-03-19, the Ember team noticed that the scheduler's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-03-19 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2026-03-19-2]
- The root cause of INC-2025-004 was a consumer offset stuck after a broker restart. [valid 2025-02-11 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-004]
- The notifier's flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during its outages. [valid 2025-02-20 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-02-20]
- As of 2025-10-15, the scheduler is owned by Team Dune, which took it over from Team Atlas. [valid 2025-10-15 to now; recorded by handover/2025-10-15-scheduler]
    earlier: As of 2025-08-29, the scheduler is owned by Team Atlas, which took it over from the Ember team. [valid 2025-09-05 to 2025-10-15; recorded by handover/2025-09-05-scheduler-correction]
    earlier: As of 2025-08-29, the scheduler is owned by Team Cinder, which took it over from the Ember team. [valid 2025-08-29 to 2025-09-05; recorded by handover/2025-08-29-scheduler]
    earlier: The scheduler is owned by the Ember team. [valid 2025-01-20 to 2025-08-29; recorded by standup/ember/2025-01-20]

Question: Who was responsible for the scheduler on 2025-09-29?

message.reasoning:
The question asks about who was responsible for the scheduler on 2025-09-29.

Looking at the memory entries about scheduler ownership:
- The scheduler is owned by the Ember team. [valid 2025-01-20 to 2025-08-29]
- As of 2025-08-29, the scheduler is owned by Team Cinder, which took it over from the Ember team. [valid 2025-08-29 to 2025-09-05]
- As of 2025-08-29, the scheduler is owned by Team Atlas, which took it over from the Ember team. [valid 2025-09-05 to 2025-10-15; recorded by handover/2025-09-05-scheduler-correction]
- As of 2025-10-15, the scheduler is owned by Team Dune, which took it over from Team Atlas. [valid 2025-10-15 to now]

For 2025-09-29:
- Team Cinder entry: valid 2025-08-29 to 2025-09-05 — does not cover 2025-09-29.
- Team Atlas correction: valid 2025-09-05 to 2025-10-15 — covers 2025-09-29.
- Team Dune: valid 2025-10-15 to now — does not cover 2025-09-29.

So on 2025-09-29, the scheduler was owned by Team Atlas (per the correction entry).
